description: Shapes more than one contract carries, written to exercise every serde attribute the generator emits.

This file exists so that two expansions of it can be compared on the wire. One shape carries an absent-able key, a nullable key, a defaulted key, a safe integer, a closed set whose wire spelling is not its Rust name, and an internally tagged union — which between them are every place the generated serde form could differ from the manifest's. If a copy generated by `imports { "demo.shared/1" => inline }` and one generated from this manifest in its own module ever disagreed, it would show up in one of these.

types.name: Envelope
description: One thing passed between peers, with a key in every state the format distinguishes.

fields.name: at_ms
description: When it was made, in milliseconds since the epoch. Exact in every target, which is what the keyword promises.

fields.name: kind
description: What sort of envelope it is.

fields.name: body
description: What it carries. Reached from here and never listed in an import, which is how the inline mode is made to bring a shape nobody wrote down.

fields.name: note
description: Anything the sender wanted to add. Absent, not null, when there was nothing.

fields.name: cause
description: What prompted this, or null when nothing did. The key is written either way, which is the difference from `note`.

fields.name: hops
description: How many relays this may still pass through. An absent key means three, which is not what `u32::default()` would give.

types.name: Kind
description: What sort of envelope this is. An unrecognised tag is a decoding failure at the boundary, not a value to carry.

variants.name: partial
description: Part of something, with more to come.

types.name: Body
description: What an envelope carries, discriminated by a key beside the rest.

variants.name: empty
description: Nothing at all, which is a body and not an absence of one.
